pages.caption: [Of all the queen's many children, only one daughter was left—but she was worth a thousand]
pages.characters: Queen
pages.scene: Once upon a time there lived a queen who had been the mother of a great many children, and of them all only one daughter was left. But then she was worth at least a thousand.

pages.caption: [The queen spoiled her daughter terribly and never corrected any of her faults]
pages.characters: Queen, Princess
pages.scene: Since the death of the King her father, the Queen had nothing in the world she cared for so much as this little Princess. She was so terribly afraid of losing her that she quite spoiled her, and never tried to correct any of her faults.

pages.caption: [She grew up so proud and so much in love with her own beauty that she despised everyone]
pages.characters: Princess
pages.scene: The little person, who was as pretty as possible and was one day to wear a crown, grew up so proud and so much in love with her own beauty that she despised everyone else in the world.

pages.caption: [The queen sent the princess's portrait to neighboring kings, and every one of them fell in love]
pages.characters: Queen, Princess, Painters
pages.scene: The Queen caused her portrait to be taken by the cleverest painters and sent it to several neighboring kings. When they saw this portrait they fell in love with the Princess, every one of them, but upon each it had a different effect.

pages.caption: [One fell ill, one went crazy, and the luckiest became her slaves the moment they saw her]
pages.characters: Kings
pages.scene: One king fell ill, one went quite crazy, and a few of the luckiest set off to see her as soon as possible. These poor princes became her slaves the moment they set eyes on her.

pages.caption: [Twenty kings exhausted every artifice to please her, but the princess was not to be won]
pages.characters: Twenty Kings
pages.scene: Never has there been a gayer Court. Twenty delightful kings did everything they could think of to make themselves agreeable. But after they had exhausted every other artifice they one and all sat down and wept, for the Princess was not to be won.

pages.caption: [A hideous dwarf with a long green beard and hump on his back arrived—the richest prince in the world]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: While the twenty kings were sighing and lamenting, a hideous little dwarf with a long green beard and a hump on his back arrived at court. He was the richest prince in the world, yet his riches had not been able to procure him a wife.

pages.caption: [He fell in love with the portrait and offered all his riches to the queen for her hand]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Queen
pages.scene: As soon as he saw the portrait of Princess Bellissima, he fell in love with her and nothing would satisfy him but to marry her at once. He offered to give up all his riches to the Queen.

pages.caption: [The queen was so dazzled by the dwarf's riches she accepted him as her son-in-law]
pages.characters: Queen, Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: The Queen had already given her word to the twenty kings, but she was so dazzled at the immense offer of the Yellow Dwarf that she accepted him for her son-in-law.

pages.caption: [The princess shut herself up in her own apartments and would not see anyone]
pages.characters: Princess
pages.scene: As soon as the Princess Bellissima heard the news she was quite beside herself with anger. She shut herself up in her own apartments and would not see anyone.

pages.caption: "If you do not marry the Yellow Dwarf I will kill you."
pages.characters: Queen, Princess
pages.scene: The Queen her mother came and wept and raged by turns, and threatened to kill her if she did not marry the Yellow Dwarf. So the poor Princess had to submit.

pages.caption: [She was married to the hideous dwarf and taken to his dismal castle]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Princess
pages.scene: The Princess was married to the hideous little dwarf. He took her away to his own country, and there she lived in a dismal castle with no one to speak to but his ugly sisters.

pages.caption: [The yellow dwarf was so jealous he never let her go outside the doors]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Princess
pages.scene: The Yellow Dwarf was so jealous of her that he never let her go outside the doors, and would not let anyone enter unless he was with her.

pages.caption: [A young king came to the dwarf's country and fell deeply in love with Bellissima]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: Now one day there came a young King to the dwarf's country, who had never seen anyone so beautiful as Bellissima. He fell deeply in love with her and at once set about planning how to rescue her.

pages.caption: [He sent a secret message, and she promised that if he could carry her off, she would marry him]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: The young King managed to send a secret message to the Princess, and she sent one back to him promising that if he could find the means of carrying her off, she would marry him.

pages.caption: [They planned to dress the princess in servant's clothes and send her to the garden]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Nurse, Princess
pages.scene: The young King and the Princess's old nurse between them planned how to get her away. The nurse was to dress the Princess in servant's clothes and send her to the garden, where the young King would be waiting for her.

pages.caption: [The dwarf had a spy watching, and he came rushing home in a fury]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Spy
pages.scene: The Yellow Dwarf had put a spy to watch the Princess, and as soon as he heard what was going on he came rushing home in a fury.

pages.caption: [The dwarf flew into a rage and called upon all his evil spirits to help him]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: He met the Princess and the young King in the garden, and seeing them together he flew into such a rage that he called upon all his evil spirits to help him.

pages.caption: [The sky grew dark, the earth shook, and frightful figures appeared in the air]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Evil Spirits
pages.scene: The sky grew dark, the earth shook, and the sea boiled, and a host of frightful figures appeared in the air. The young King fought bravely, but the evil spirits were too strong for him.

pages.caption: [The Fairy of the Desert appeared upon a griffin and struck the princess with her lance]
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, Princess, Queen
pages.scene: Just when all seemed lost, the Fairy of the Desert appeared upon a terrible griffin. She struck the Princess with a lance she carried, and Bellissima fell into the Queen's arms bleeding and senseless.

pages.caption: [The dwarf snatched Bellissima from the queen's arms and disappeared with his prize]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Princess, Queen
pages.scene: The young King, seeing his beloved Princess struck down, gave up the combat. But the Yellow Dwarf snatched Bellissima from the Queen's arms and sprang upon the roof of the palace and disappeared with his prize.

pages.caption: [The king looked on in horror, powerless to prevent it, and felt himself carried through the air]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The young King, motionless with horror, looked on despairingly at this dreadful occurrence, which he was quite powerless to prevent. Everything became dark, and he felt himself carried along through the air by a strong hand.

pages.caption: [She chained him to a rock in a frightful cavern, hoping he would forget Bellissima]
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The Fairy of the Desert had fallen in love with the handsome young King the moment she saw him. She carried him off to a frightful cavern and chained him to a rock, hoping the fear of death would make him forget Bellissima.

pages.caption: "What do I see? Is it you, dear Prince? What misfortune has brought you here?"
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Then she appeared before him as a young and beautiful fairy, and pretended to have come there quite by chance. "What do I see?" she cried. "Is it you, dear Prince?"

pages.caption: "Alas! beautiful Fairy, the fairy who brought me here first took away my sight."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The King, quite deceived by her altered appearance, replied that the fairy who brought him here first took away his sight, but by her voice he recognized her as the Fairy of the Desert.

pages.caption: "If you have fallen into her hands, you won't get away until you have married her."
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert
pages.scene: "Ah!" cried the pretended Fairy, "if you have fallen into her hands, you won't get away until you have married her. She has carried off more than one Prince like this."

pages.caption: "If the Fairy should set me free my gratitude would oblige me to love her only."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Without seeming to have noticed anything, the King said he had no dislike to the Fairy of the Desert, but he could not endure the way she protected the Yellow Dwarf. It was true he loved a charming princess, but if she should set him free his gratitude would oblige him to love her only.

pages.caption: "Do you really mean what you say, Prince?" "Surely."
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "Do you really mean what you say, Prince?" said the Fairy, quite deceived. "Surely," replied the Prince; "how could I deceive you?"

pages.caption: [She harnessed swans to her chariot instead of the usual bats]
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The Fairy of the Desert, quite taken in by these words, resolved at once to transport the Prince to a pleasanter place. She made him mount her chariot, to which she had harnessed swans instead of the bats which generally drew it.

pages.caption: [He saw Bellissima in a castle of polished steel whose walls reflected the sun so hotly no one could approach]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: Away she flew with him. But imagine the distress of the Prince when, from the giddy height, he saw his beloved Princess in a castle built of polished steel, the walls of which reflected the sun's rays so hotly that no one could approach without being burnt to a cinder.

pages.caption: [Bellissima sat by a brook weeping bitterly, and looked up to see the king and the fairy]
pages.characters: Princess, King of the Gold Mines, Fairy of the Desert
pages.scene: Bellissima was sitting in a little thicket by a brook, leaning her head upon her hand and weeping bitterly. Just as they passed she looked up and saw the King and the Fairy of the Desert.

pages.caption: "Was I not unhappy enough? Must I also know that the King of the Gold Mines ceased to love me?"
pages.characters: Princess
pages.scene: "What!" she cried; "was I not unhappy enough in this lonely castle to which that frightful Yellow Dwarf brought me? Must I also be made to know that the King of the Gold Mines ceased to love me?"

pages.caption: [The king loved her as much as ever and was terribly sad, but knew he must use patience and cunning]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The King really loved her as much as ever, and was feeling terribly sad at being so rapidly torn away from his beloved Princess. But he knew too well how powerful the Fairy was to have any hope of escaping except by great patience and cunning.

pages.caption: "You are so much more to me than she is that I would rather die than leave you."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "No one can tell you what you wish to know better than I can," said he. "This chance meeting with an unhappy princess for whom I once had a passing fancy has affected me a little, but you are so much more to me than she is that I would rather die than leave you."

pages.caption: "Can I believe that you really love me so much?" "Time will show, madam."
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "Ah, Prince," she said, "can I believe that you really love me so much?" "Time will show, madam," replied the King. The Fairy of the Desert was delighted to hear them sing of her triumphs.

pages.caption: [They reached a vast meadow with a splendid palace whose walls were of transparent emeralds]
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: They reached a vast meadow, gay with all sorts of flowers. A deep river surrounded it, and many little brooks murmured softly under the shady trees. A little way off stood a splendid palace, the walls of which were of transparent emeralds.

pages.caption: [He was given a splendid room and left alone, but suspected the fairy was watching]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The King was given a room most splendidly furnished, and left alone for a little while. He felt sure the Fairy had not really gone quite away, but was watching him from some hiding-place.

pages.caption: "Trusty counsellor, let me see what I can do to please the charming Fairy of the Desert."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: So walking up to a great mirror, he said to it, "Trusty counsellor, let me see what I can do to make myself agreeable to the charming Fairy of the Desert; for I can think of nothing but how to please her."

pages.caption: [He curled his hair and put on a grander coat, and the fairy returned delighted]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Fairy of the Desert
pages.scene: He at once set to work to curl his hair, and seeing upon a table a grander coat than his own he put it on carefully. The Fairy came back so delighted that she could not conceal her joy.

pages.caption: "I am quite aware of the trouble you have taken to please me. You have succeeded perfectly."
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "I am quite aware of the trouble you have taken to please me," said she. "And I must tell you that you have succeeded perfectly already." The King did not spare pretty speeches.

pages.caption: [She allowed him to walk on the shore, confident her terrible storm would prevent escape]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: After a time he was allowed to walk by himself upon the sea-shore. The Fairy had raised a terrible storm that the boldest pilot would not venture out in it, so she was not afraid of her prisoner's being able to escape.

pages.caption: "O! lovely nymphs, from ocean caves, come up and calm the furious waves and set a desperate lover free!"
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Presently, after walking wildly up and down, he wrote verses upon the sand with his stick, lamenting his terrible situation. He called upon the lovely nymphs from ocean caves to calm the furious waves and set a desperate lover free.

pages.caption: [A lovely lady floated toward him on a huge billow, holding a mirror and a comb]
pages.characters: Mermaid, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: While he was still writing he heard a voice which attracted his attention. He saw a lovely lady floating gently toward him upon the crest of a huge billow, her long hair spread all about her. In one hand she held a mirror, and in the other a comb.

pages.caption: [Instead of feet she had a beautiful tail like a fish, with which she swam]
pages.characters: Mermaid, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Instead of feet she had a beautiful tail like a fish, with which she swam. The King was struck dumb with astonishment at this unexpected sight.

pages.caption: "If you like I will help you to escape from this fatal place."
pages.characters: Mermaid
pages.scene: As soon as she came within speaking distance, she said to him: "I know how sad you are at losing your Princess and being kept a prisoner by the Fairy of the Desert; if you like I will help you to escape from this fatal place."

pages.caption: [He hesitated, afraid this might be another trick of the Fairy of the Desert]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The King hardly knew what answer to make. Not because he did not wish very much to escape, but he was afraid that this might be only another device of the Fairy of the Desert to deceive him.

pages.caption: "You may trust me. I am so angry with the Yellow Dwarf and the Fairy of the Desert."
pages.characters: Mermaid
pages.scene: "You may trust me," said the Mermaid. "I am not trying to entrap you. I am so angry with the Yellow Dwarf and the Fairy of the Desert that I am not likely to wish to help them."

pages.caption: "I trust you absolutely. Tell me how my Princess is."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Mermaid
pages.scene: "I trust you absolutely," cried the King. He begged her to tell him how his Princess was. The Mermaid said they must not waste time in talking—she would carry him to the Castle of Steel.

pages.caption: "My friendly sea-weeds, stay here until the Fairy of the Desert comes."
pages.characters: Mermaid
pages.scene: So saying, she collected a bundle of sea-weed, and blowing it three times, she said: "My friendly sea-weeds, I order you to stay here stretched upon the sand until the Fairy of the Desert comes to take you away."

pages.caption: [The sea-weeds became like the king, pale and still on the sand]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Sea-weeds
pages.scene: At once the sea-weeds became like the King, who stood looking at them in great astonishment, for they were even dressed in a coat like his, but they lay there pale and still.

pages.caption: [The mermaid caught up the king and swam joyfully away with him]
pages.characters: Mermaid, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Then the Mermaid caught up the King and away they swam joyfully together. She told him about the Princess—the Yellow Dwarf had compelled her to mount behind him on his terrible Spanish cat.

pages.caption: "Armed with it you may dare any danger, but never let it fall from your hand."
pages.characters: Mermaid, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: She gave to the King a sword made from a single diamond, which was more brilliant than the sun. She told him armed with it he might dare any danger, but he must never let it fall from his hand.

pages.caption: [He thanked the mermaid and set out, longing to see Bellissima]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The King thanked the Mermaid and set out for the Castle of Steel. He walked fast, looking anxiously round him, and longing once more to see his darling Bellissima.

pages.caption: [He was surrounded by four terrible sphinxes who would have torn him to pieces]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Sphinxes
pages.scene: But he had not gone far before he was surrounded by four terrible sphinxes who would very soon have torn him to pieces with their sharp talons.

pages.caption: [He flashed the diamond sword and the sphinxes fell helpless at his feet]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Sphinxes
pages.scene: For no sooner had he flashed the diamond sword before their eyes than down they fell at his feet quite helpless, and he killed them with one blow.

pages.caption: [He met six dragons covered with scales harder than iron]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Dragons
pages.scene: He had hardly turned to continue his search when he met six dragons covered with scales that were harder than iron. Frightful as this encounter was, the King's courage was unshaken.

pages.caption: [By the aid of his sword he cut the dragons in pieces one after the other]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Dragons
pages.scene: By the aid of his wonderful sword he cut them in pieces one after the other. Now he hoped his difficulties were over, but at the next turning he was met by one which he did not know how to overcome.

pages.caption: "Where are you going, Prince? If we let you pass great misfortunes will happen."
pages.characters: Nymphs, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: Four-and-twenty pretty and graceful nymphs advanced toward him, holding garlands of flowers, with which they barred the way. "Where are you going, Prince?" they said.

pages.caption: [He hesitated, knowing it was wrong to harm a lady, but a voice whispered in his ear]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Nymphs
pages.scene: The King did not know what to do or to say. It went against all his ideas as a knight to do anything a lady begged him not to do; but as he hesitated a voice in his ear said:

pages.caption: "Strike! strike! and do not spare, or your Princess is lost for ever!"
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Nymphs
pages.scene: "Strike! strike! and do not spare, or your Princess is lost for ever!" So without reply to the nymphs he rushed forward instantly, breaking their garlands, and scattering them in all directions.

pages.caption: [He reached the little wood where Bellissima sat pale and weary by the brook]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: He went on without further hindrance to the little wood where he had seen Bellissima. She was seated by the brook looking pale and weary when he reached her.

pages.caption: [She drew herself away with as much indignation as if he had been the Yellow Dwarf]
pages.characters: Princess, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: He would have thrown himself down at her feet, but she drew herself away from him with as much indignation as if he had been the Yellow Dwarf.

pages.caption: "Did I not see you flying through the air with the loveliest being imaginable?"
pages.characters: Princess, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "Ah! Princess," he cried, "do not be angry with me. Let me explain everything." "Ah!" cried Bellissima, "did I not see you flying through the air with the loveliest being imaginable?"

pages.caption: "The wicked Fairy of the Desert carried me off in her chariot to the other end of the earth."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: "Indeed it was, Princess," he answered. "The wicked Fairy of the Desert, not content with chaining me to a rock, carried me off in her chariot to the other end of the earth."

pages.caption: [He threw himself at her feet and let fall the sword, which the dwarf seized]
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess, Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: He threw himself at her feet and held her by her robe. But alas! in so doing he let fall the magic sword, and the Yellow Dwarf, who was crouching behind a lettuce, no sooner saw it than he sprang out and seized it.

pages.caption: [The dwarf muttered magical words and summoned two giants who bound the king in chains]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Princess, King of the Gold Mines, Giants
pages.scene: The Princess gave a cry of terror on seeing the Dwarf, but this only irritated the little monster. Muttering a few magical words he summoned two giants, who bound the King with great chains of iron.

pages.caption: "I will give him his life if you, Princess, will consent to marry me."
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, Princess
pages.scene: "Now," said the Dwarf, "I am master of my rival's fate, but I will give him his life and permission to depart unharmed if you, Princess, will consent to marry me."

pages.caption: "Let me die a thousand times rather."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: "Let me die a thousand times rather," cried the unhappy King. "Alas!" cried the Princess, "must you die? Could anything be more terrible?"

pages.caption: "Let me have the satisfaction of dying for you, my Princess."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Princess
pages.scene: "That you should marry that little wretch would be far more terrible," answered the King. "At least," continued she, "let us die together." "Let me have the satisfaction of dying for you, my Princess," said he.

pages.caption: "Oh, no, no! Rather than that I will do as you wish."
pages.characters: Princess, Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: "Oh, no, no!" she cried, turning to the Dwarf. "Rather than that I will do as you wish."

pages.caption: "You are a rival of whom I am too much afraid; you shall not see our marriage."
pages.characters: King of the Gold Mines, Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: "Cruel Princess!" said the King. "Would you make my life horrible to me by marrying another before my eyes?" "Not so," replied the Yellow Dwarf. "You are a rival of whom I am too much afraid; you shall not see our marriage."

pages.caption: [The dwarf stabbed the king to the heart with the diamond sword]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: So saying, in spite of Bellissima's tears and cries, he stabbed the King to the heart with the diamond sword.

pages.caption: [She sank down beside him and died of a broken heart]
pages.characters: Princess, King of the Gold Mines
pages.scene: The poor Princess, seeing her lover lying dead at her feet, could no longer live without him; she sank down by him and died of a broken heart.

pages.caption: [They could not be helped, for all magic power had been lost with the diamond sword]
pages.characters: Mermaid
pages.scene: So ended these unfortunate lovers, whom not even the Mermaid could help, because all the magic power had been lost with the diamond sword.

pages.caption: [The dwarf preferred to see the princess dead rather than married to the king]
pages.characters: Yellow Dwarf
pages.scene: As to the wicked Dwarf, he preferred to see the Princess dead rather than married to the King of the Gold Mines.

pages.caption: [She pulled down the monument and hated him as much as she had loved him]
pages.characters: Fairy of the Desert
pages.scene: The Fairy of the Desert, when she heard of the King's adventures, pulled down the grand monument which she had built, and was so angry at the trick that had been played her that she hated him as much as she had loved him before.

pages.caption: [The mermaid changed them into two tall palm trees, whispering together of their faithful love]
pages.characters: Mermaid
pages.scene: The kind Mermaid, grieved at the sad fate of the lovers, caused them to be changed into two tall palm trees, which stand always side by side, whispering together of their faithful love and caressing one another with their interlacing branches.
